description: One Word Substitution means expressing a long sentence or phrase with just a single, exact word. It makes vocabulary concise and effective, and it is a crucial part of competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts and Root Word Method
sections.description: Most words in the English language are derived from Latin or Greek roots. By identifying the root word, we can accurately guess the meaning of unfamiliar words.

key_concepts.explanation: This is the core part of a word that determines its basic meaning. Example: 'Auto' means 'Self'.
Syllables added at the beginning (Prefix) or at the end (Suffix) of a word change its meaning and grammatical category. Example: 'Phobia' (Fear) is a suffix.

sections.title: Words Denoting Killings (Cide)
sections.description: The suffix 'Cide' means killing or killer. New words are formed by attaching various root words to this suffix.

examples.incorrect_or_context: The act of killing one's own father
The act of killing a king
The murder of a whole race or group of people

sections.title: Words Denoting Government (Cracy/Archy)
sections.description: The suffix 'Cracy' or 'Archy' refers to a system of rule or government.

examples.incorrect_or_context: A government by the wealthy or rich people
A government run by a few people
A state of disorder due to absence of authority or government

sections.title: Words Denoting Fears (Phobia)
sections.description: The suffix 'Phobia' means an extreme and irrational fear of a specific object, situation, or person.

examples.incorrect_or_context: Extreme or irrational fear of heights
Fear of confined or closed spaces

sections.title: Strategies for Solving in Exams
sections.description: Effective methods to accurately solve multiple-choice questions based on one-word substitution in competitive exams.

strategies.title: Identify the Root Word
strategies.detail: Understand the main idea of the given phrase. If the question states 'love for mankind', look for the roots 'Phil' (Love) and 'Anthro' (Mankind) in the given options to find 'Philanthropist'.

strategies.title: Process of Elimination
strategies.detail: Eliminate the options whose suffix or prefix completely mismatches the context of the question.

strategies.title: Tone Analysis of the Word
strategies.detail: Identify whether the tone of the phrase is positive, negative, or neutral. For example, for 'Hater of women', choose the option with the negative prefix 'Miso' (Misogynist).
